aboutH2: Carrier Sekani Family Services: Substance Use Recovery Program in Vanderhoof, BC
intro: Carrier Sekani Family Services (CSFS) is a non-profit society created in 1990 under the guidance of the Carrier Sekani Tribal Council. It runs health, child and family, justice and research services for its Member Nations, and this page covers only its addiction and mental wellness work. That work centres on the Substance Use Recovery Program (SURP), run from the Vanderhoof office. In plain terms, SURP offers short residential treatment at Ormond Lake from May to October, community-based programs of one or two weeks across northern BC from November to April, and individual counselling and after-care in between. It is not a year-round treatment centre, and CSFS does not describe any detox service.

The integrated Mental Health and Addictions Program, “Lhet’sut’en” is delivered by our multi-disciplinary team. During the summer months (from May to October), we operate the Ormond Lake Cultural Healing Camp on Nadleh Whut’en territory. Focusing on the holistic well-being of members, this program offers cultural healing combined with Western therapies. Camp themes include “Reclaiming Ourselves”, “Journey to Hope”, and “New Horizons”. During the winter months (November to April), our team visits member communities, offering educational workshops and other support services when requested. This program is a great example of the integration of Tradition and Western treatment strategies, which is reflective of our program’s vision statement: Culture is Healing.

pillars.title: Ormond Lake in Summer, Home Communities in Winter
pillars.body: SURP's residential treatment runs at Ormond Lake on Nadleh Whut’en territory, west of Vanderhoof, during the summer months from May to October. CSFS calls the site the Ormond Lake Healing Centre. From November to April the team travels instead, bringing one-week or two-week programs, workshops and education sessions to communities across northern BC when a Nation asks for them. Winter topics listed by CSFS include addiction and wellness, self-esteem, family violence, shame and guilt, spirituality, and gambling and other behavioural addictions. Day-to-day contact happens through the Vanderhoof office on West Stewart Street, open weekdays from 8:30 to 4:30.

pillars.title: Culture and Clinical Counselling Together
pillars.body: CSFS says SURP brings clinical counsellors, cultural knowledge holders and Wellness Workers together to blend evidence-based addiction treatment with Carrier and Sekani traditions, land-based practices and community connection. The program describes healing through connection to land, teachings and ceremony, cultural identity and belonging, and community relationships, alongside trauma-informed clinical counselling. A 2026 update from CSFS described a two-week program at Ormond Lake with smudging, beadwork, drum making, dream catchers and land-based activities, guided by Knowledge Keepers and Atsoos (grandmothers). The same summer it ran a two-week Trauma Recovery Program covering grief and loss, emotional safety, healthy relationships and coping strategies.

pillars.title: After-Care, Wellbriety and Local Wellness Workers
pillars.body: Support continues after a residential stay. SURP lists after-care and relapse prevention, individual counselling, and Wellbriety sessions held in person or online. Wellness Workers based in Prince George and Burns Lake give local support, and Mental Health and Wellness Services offers free counselling to people from CSFS Member Nations, with offices in Prince George and Vanderhoof. CSFS is also building the Tachick Lake Healing Centre, which it says will run year-round with detox, cultural and clinical treatment and aftercare. It was still under construction in mid-2026, so it is not open yet.

overviewH2: Carrier Sekani Family Services: Mental Health and Wellness
overview: Alongside SURP, CSFS runs Mental Health and Wellness Services for children, youth and adults from its Member Nations. The team includes Master’s-level Mental Health Clinicians and Mental Health Support Workers. They offer assessment and counselling, individual and group therapy in person or online, crisis support during core hours when it is feasible, workshops, and referrals to specialised services. Services are free, and CSFS describes its intake as “every door is the right door”: you can start anywhere and staff will help you find the right support.

location.heading: Carrier Sekani Family Services in Vanderhoof, British Columbia
location.intro: The Substance Use Recovery Program is run from the CSFS office on West Stewart Street in Vanderhoof, in the Nechako Valley of Northern BC, while summer residential treatment happens at Ormond Lake on Nadleh Whut’en territory to the west. From Vancouver it is a long trip: about 9 hours by road, or a flight to Prince George and then about an hour and a quarter west on Highway 16. Fort St. James is under an hour north, Fraser Lake about 45 minutes west and Burns Lake about 1 hour 45 minutes west.

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's listing and its own website. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: What level of care does Carrier Sekani Family Services offer for addiction?
faqs.a: CSFS offers seasonal residential treatment plus community-based and outpatient support, through its Substance Use Recovery Program (SURP). Residential programs run at Ormond Lake from May to October, and from November to April the team runs one-week or two-week programs and workshops in communities across northern BC. Individual counselling, Wellbriety sessions and after-care run alongside.

faqs.q: Who can attend the Substance Use Recovery Program?
faqs.a: SURP is for Indigenous adults (Status, Inuit or Métis) who live in British Columbia or the Yukon. Participants must be able to take part in group-based treatment. Under First Nations Health Authority policy, CSFS cannot accept clients from other provinces.

faqs.q: How much does the program cost?
faqs.a: CSFS says its programs are funded for Indigenous clients, and it publishes no fees. Travel and related supports follow First Nations Health Authority (FNHA) policies, so ask your counsellor or the SURP front desk how travel to Ormond Lake would be covered.

faqs.q: How do I apply for treatment at Ormond Lake?
faqs.a: Start with a mental health professional, who completes or reviews the Treatment Centre Application with you. CSFS asks for at least six one-hour pre-treatment counselling or support sessions, TB screening and a medical assessment before you go. Once the application is sent by email or fax, you receive a letter of acceptance and arrange travel.

faqs.q: Does Carrier Sekani Family Services offer detox?
faqs.a: No detox service is listed on the CSFS website today, and recovery.com's profile says the program has no medically supervised withdrawal. If you need to withdraw from alcohol or drugs first, talk to your doctor or counsellor about a detox bed before applying. CSFS says its Tachick Lake Healing Centre, still under construction in 2026, will include detox when it opens.

Programs are short. CSFS lists one-week and two-week treatment programs in winter, and its 2026 summer programs at Ormond Lake ran for two weeks. Ask the front desk which sessions are open when you apply.

faqs.q: Where is the program and how do I get there?
faqs.a: The program office is at 240 West Stewart Street in Vanderhoof, in the Nechako Valley of Northern BC, and summer treatment takes place at Ormond Lake on Nadleh Whut’en territory. Vanderhoof is about an hour and a quarter west of Prince George on Highway 16 and about 9 hours by road from Vancouver. Once you are accepted, you make your own travel arrangements to and from the program.

faqs.q: What support is there after treatment?
faqs.a: SURP offers after-care and relapse prevention, individual counselling and Wellbriety sessions in person or online. Wellness Workers in Prince George and Burns Lake can give local support, and people from CSFS Member Nations can use the free Mental Health and Wellness Services.

faqs.q: Does CSFS offer mental health counselling as well?
faqs.a: Yes. CSFS Mental Health and Wellness Services offers free assessment, counselling and group therapy, in person or online, for children, youth and adults from its Member Nations. Referrals go to communitymhreferral@csfs.org for adults and cymhreferral@csfs.org for children and youth aged 6 to 19.

faqs.q: How do I contact the Substance Use Recovery Program?
faqs.a: Call the SURP front desk at 250-567-2900 or email surp@csfs.org. The Vanderhoof office is open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and programming hours change with the season. The Vanderhoof office also has a toll-free line, 1-866-567-2333.
